text: Highlights the role of diet in preventing malnutrition and NCDs; stresses early‑life dietary habits.
Defines adequacy, balance, moderation and diversity as foundations of a healthy diet.
Recommends unrefined carbohydrates as major energy sources; encourages whole grains, vegetables, fruits and pulses.
age_range: All ages; specific values for 2–9 and 10+

text: Recommends ≥400 g/day for adults; lower amounts for children (250–350 g depending on age).
Recommends ≥25 g/day for adults; lower amounts for children (15–21 g depending on age).
Advises limiting free sugars to <10% of energy intake; <5% provides additional benefits.
Recommends limiting total fat to <30% of energy; saturated fat <10%; trans fat <1%; emphasises unsaturated fats.
Suggests 10–15% of energy from protein; higher needs in adolescence and active individuals.
Recommends <5 g/day salt for adults; lower for children; encourages potassium‑rich foods.
Emphasises importance of vitamins and minerals; highlights global deficiency prevalence.
Recommends exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months; continued breastfeeding to 2 years; no added salt/sugar in complementary foods.
Describes how social, economic and environmental factors shape diets; calls for multisectoral action.
Lists evidence‑based actions for governments to promote healthy diets (taxes, reformulation, school standards).
Summarises WHO’s global strategies, guidelines and monitoring systems for improving diets.
